system_overview: This specification further refines the PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) model by distinguishing between different lengths of DNA molecules produced during amplification. In real PCR, the first few cycles produce DNA strands of varying lengths because polymerase extends primers to the end of the template. Only after several cycles does the target-length product (bounded by both primer sites) begin to accumulate exponentially. This specification tracks long, short, and target-length variants of templates, hybrids, and double-stranded DNA separately, providing a high-resolution view of PCR amplification dynamics.
actors_and_components: The system has no concurrent actors. It models a single PCR reaction vessel. The molecular components are classified by length: long templates (original-length single strands), short templates (one-primer-bounded), and target-length (tiny) templates (bounded by both primers), with corresponding hybrid and double-stranded categories. The desired product is the target-length double-stranded DNA.
state_variables: The system tracks fifteen quantities: (1) temperature phase; (2) stage indicator (initial, denatured, ready, annealed, extended); (3) cycle counter; (4) available primer count; (5-7) three categories of single-stranded templates: long, short, and target-length; (8-10) three categories of primer-template hybrids: long, short, and target-length; (11-14) four categories of double-stranded DNA: long-long (original), short-long, target-short, and target-target (the desired product).
initial_state: Temperature is at extension level. Stage is initial. Cycle counter is zero. Primer count equals the initial constant. The long-long double-stranded DNA count equals the initial DNA constant. All other molecular counts (all template types, all hybrid types, short-long doubles, target-short doubles, and product) are zero.
actions: Four actions model the PCR cycle with length-differentiated molecular tracking: (1) Heating: denatures all four double-strand categories and all three hybrid categories into their component single strands. Long-long doubles produce two long templates; short-long doubles produce one long and one short template; target-short doubles produce one short and one target-length template; product doubles produce two target-length templates. Primers are recovered from all denatured hybrids. (2) Cooling: lowers temperature from denaturation to ready. No molecular changes. (3) Annealing: primers bind to available templates. A nondeterministic total number of primers are consumed, distributed across the three template categories. Each template type produces the corresponding hybrid type. (4) Extension: each long hybrid becomes a short-long double-strand, each short hybrid becomes a target-short double-strand, and each target-length hybrid becomes a product molecule. The cycle counter increments.
safety_properties: Type correctness: all molecular counts, temperature, stage, and cycle counter are within their expected domains. No target-length product is produced before the third cycle.
liveness_properties: Primer depletion: eventually all primers are consumed (inherited from the stages refinement via a refinement mapping).
model_bounds: Initial DNA and primer counts are declared as constants. For model checking, typical values are 5 for each. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on all four actions. This module refines the stages specification: a refinement mapping shows that the sum of all template types corresponds to the template count in the stages model, and similarly for hybrids and double-strands. The key insight modeled is that target-length product only begins to appear after two full cycles of amplification, as short templates must first be created from long templates before target-length strands can emerge.
